idiom_name: pthread_mutex-protected state struct + CLOCK_MONOTONIC cooldown + counter window
implementation_notes: C has no breaker library and no runtime to lean on, so the pattern is a struct plus a few functions: a state enum (closed/open/half-open), counters for failures and total calls, an int64 cooldown deadline computed from clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC), and admission/recording helpers guarded by a pthread_mutex (or by C11 atomic counters with the transition done under the lock). Nothing replaces the classic structure here, so the classic form is always the choice; the real decisions are placement - one struct instance per dependency, initialized explicitly rather than hidden in a singleton - and keeping the protected call outside the lock so the breaker never serializes the dependency. Return a distinct status code for the short circuit (CB_OPEN versus the driver's error) so callers can branch instead of parsing errno.
pitfalls: The cooldown must come from CLOCK_MONOTONIC; CLOCK_REALTIME (or time(NULL)) follows the wall clock and can open or close the circuit at the wrong moment.
The breaker lock must cover only state and counters, never the protected call, or every request serializes behind one mutex.
A breaker struct copied per thread stops aggregating failures (each copy sees only its own calls), which silently disables tripping; share it by reference.
Emitting logs or metrics callbacks while holding the breaker lock invites deadlock whenever the callback re-enters the breaker.
Counters of type int incremented from several threads race; use C11 atomics or keep every update under the same mutex.
